about: The design log: every design decision, what was tried, what Pritam picked and why. Retired variants live in git at `archive` (tagged design-log/<id>); scripts/design-log-all.mjs photographs them into <id>/sheet.jpg. Live variants are still in Storybook (`live`). Nothing tried is deleted from history.

entries.title: The Add details card
entries.question: What should the card that opens after a save look like?
entries.tried: Five redesigns of the old card (a quiet sheet first), then a Refined card in five treatments (soft pills, icon pills, sections, inline save, a text line) and five ways to share to a collection (just the pill, a caption line, a small block, a preview, in the list).
entries.picked: Refined: the title and note edited in place with nothing above the title, folder and tags as pills, My library and Share beside Save; sharing adds one caption line.
entries.why: Pritam: cards with nothing above the title, and pills instead of fields.

entries.title: From card controls to a design system
entries.question: Are “pill”, “chip” and “card controls” a design system?
entries.tried: The card's parts as one-off controls: buttons, a title and note, a list picker, a pill, a tag chip.
entries.picked: Named components with variants and sizes in one shared stylesheet — Card, Button, Select, Tag, Badge, Text field, Listbox, Status message, Tooltip — on scale tokens for space, radius, controls, text and shadow.
entries.why: Pritam: it can't be just card controls, pill, chip; use proper terms, variants, one system for the whole product.

entries.title: Previewing the save, and its sync state
entries.question: How does the card show what was saved, and whether it reached the library?
entries.tried: Banner previews in several frames, a save preview per kind, ways to show a draft's status, and where drafts collect.
entries.picked: A Framed banner preview of the save (a small WebP made by the extension, never the capture itself), one sync icon in its corner that retries or signs in, and drafts as a quiet count on the dock plus a banner above the library on the website.
entries.why: Picked in Storybook on 29 September and built the same day.

entries.title: The first screen: first ideas
entries.question: What does someone see the first time they open FoundKeep?
entries.tried: First-screen concepts with emoji objects floating round the words.
entries.picked: A direction: a sky or a meadow behind, smoother motion, and proper objects — things FoundKeep keeps — instead of emoji.
entries.why: Pritam: sky or meadow; smooth the animation; proper assets, things our app provides, not emoji.

entries.title: Rotating finds, in FoundKeep's own objects
entries.question: Which first screen, and in which type?
entries.tried: FoundKeep's own 3D objects (made in three.js), layouts round a centre bookmark, the rotating headline in Fraunces, and sky ideas.
entries.picked: Rotating finds — the headline's word changes through the things you keep — but not its font, and no bookmark in the centre.
entries.why: Pritam kept Rotating finds but not its font, and asked for no bookmark in the centre.

entries.title: Typefaces
entries.question: What is FoundKeep's typeface, and what does the headline's word wear?
entries.tried: Six pairings for the headline — Instrument Serif, DM Serif Display, Bricolage Grotesque, Unbounded, Syne, Plus Jakarta Sans with a handwritten Caveat word — and a brand-type page trying them across the product.
entries.picked: SF Pro, Apple's own typeface, as the brand font everywhere; Caveat only for the sign-in word.
entries.why: Pritam: the font Apple uses; expressive faces only for moments like sign-in and onboarding.

entries.title: Locking the sign-in screen
entries.question: Which headline, layout and sky?
entries.tried: Headline styles and layouts, twelve backdrops (meadows, alpine mornings, skies above and below the clouds), Codex's sky screens, sizes and letter-spacing, and an email sheet.
entries.picked: The Cumulus sky at blur 1; “Keep Every” in SF Pro Bold with the word in Caveat, tilted, cycling Reel, Short, Article, Tweet, Post, Thread; “All in one place, ready for your agent.” at full opacity; the Apple and Google buttons.
entries.why: Pritam tuned the size and letter-spacing himself, swapped the caption for one about the agent, then: “lock this version down”.

entries.title: Floating elements: who makes them
entries.question: Where do the floating objects come from?
entries.tried: FoundKeep's own three.js renders, and GPT-6 Astra's first set of objects.
entries.picked: Every floating element from GPT-6 Astra, with the missing ones generated: reel, short, article, tweet, thread, photo post, and the agent's orb and reply.
entries.why: Pritam wanted every element from GPT-6 Astra — and there was still no tweet, reel or short.

entries.title: Floating elements: style
entries.question: In what style do the eight objects float?
entries.tried: Six styles of the same eight objects — glass, cards, paper, cloud, photo, clay — with and without depth, and the porcelain set.
entries.picked: Cards: floating like iOS widgets, with real photos.
entries.why: The first set “looked out of place” on the sky (Pritam); of the six styles: “Cards — lock this and add this”.

entries.title: How the cards keep moving
entries.question: Once the cards arrive, how do they move?
entries.tried: Drift, spotlight on the headline's word, orbit, bob and sway, rise like bubbles.
entries.picked: Drift, in the app for now — still open.
entries.why: Not picked yet; drift is what the app uses.

entries.title: Sign-in: three versions, and a poll
entries.question: Floating cards, or a window playing a film of FoundKeep at work?
entries.tried: Version one, the floating cards over the sky; version two, a light page with a window playing an 11-second film (share a reel, it lands in one place, find it again, Kit the agent uses it); version three, that film on the sky. Six film variations, and a poll video of all three.
entries.picked: Version one, in the app. Versions two and three kept for an A/B test.
entries.why: On X, people said version one was much better.

entries.title: Apple and Google only
entries.question: Does the app keep an email sign-in?
entries.tried: The sign-in, create-account and recover screens with email and password, as they were.
entries.picked: Apple and Google only — no email anywhere in the app; if neither can be reached, say so and offer Try again.
entries.why: Pritam’s answer when asked whether email stays.

entries.title: After “Continue with Google”
entries.question: What does the app show while Google opens, waits, and signs you in?
entries.tried: The buttons become a card; a sheet over sign-in; the cards gather into a ring round Google's mark; a calm light page.
entries.picked: The cards gather — and go back to their places if it didn't finish. Then, on review: three or four words inside the ring, smaller, and a wider ring, so the cards never crowd the text.
entries.why: Pritam: “this is good”; then “they are very near the text … we don't need to write that much”.

entries.title: First run
entries.question: What does someone see right after they first sign in?
entries.tried: Watch it happen (a post goes Share → FoundKeep → into your library, on a loop); three steps (Tap Share · Pick FoundKeep · It’s kept, ready for your agent); the share sheet up close, with the iPhone step people miss (More, then add FoundKeep); try it once (share a sample post here and watch it land). Each for iPhone and Android.
entries.picked: Watch it happen — remade for the app with an X-style post (FoundKeep right in the share sheet's row) and a reel (slide to More, then FoundKeep), the iOS 26 share sheet and FoundKeep's own save sheet; each save leaves as one of the sign-in screen's floating cards. Shown once on each device after signing in. Provisional: once the other screens are designed, Pritam records the real flow and it is remade from that recording.
entries.why: Pritam: watch it happen, with better post and reel screens, FoundKeep straight from the row or through More, playing by itself — “once we are done with all of our designs of the other screens, I will record and share the video … and make it much more real”.

entries.title: The Library
entries.question: How should the place you come back to, to find what you kept, be laid out?
entries.tried: Today's “The collection.” (search, kind tabs, a masonry of mixed cards) against four layouts on a richer sample library: cards (the sign-in screen's cards, a picture and the title, nothing above it, in two columns); a grid like Photos (three across, by day, a small mark for videos, posts and links); shelves by kind (just saved, videos, to read, posts, photos, notes); and a dense list by day. Each in light and dark.
entries.picked: Today's layout, with the scroll edge (on in the app). Next: the cards — how each kind of save looks, with its platform, tags and folder, to make it clean.
entries.why: Pritam picked “Today, with the scroll edge” — and “we will work on our cards design … for each type of save … to clear out everything and make our UI clean”.

entries.title: The scroll edge: progressive blur
entries.question: What happens where content scrolls under the top bar and the dock?
entries.tried: Pritam's reference recording (an events app: a pinned header, the list blurring progressively as it slides under it, and again under a floating button at the bottom) and expo-backdrop's ProgressiveBlurView; iOS 26's own scroll edge effect (react-native-screens' scrollEdgeEffects) only works under the native navigation header, on iOS 26, and not on Android.
entries.picked: A progressive blur at the top and bottom of scrolling screens, placed as in the reference: full strength over the status bar and the pinned top bar, clearing in a short strip just below it; at the bottom, starting at the dock's middle so what's above it stays sharp. On the phone, expo-backdrop's native ProgressiveBlurView (public UIKit and Android APIs; fades in once content is under it); on the web, stacked CSS backdrop blurs. Shown on today's Library (behind a switch, off in the app until picked) and the Library proposals.
entries.why: Pritam: “now in our scroll we will have progress blur in our app”, with the recording; then “positioning of blur is wrong — show me how it will look on today's collection page”. The first try blurred too far below the bar and started well above the dock.

entries.title: Cards for every kind of save
entries.question: How should each kind of save look in the Library — with where it came from, its tags and its folder — so the cards are clean?
entries.tried: Today's card (a source chip over the picture, the title, folder, hashtags, “iPhone · 3d ago”, status lines) against three that share one order — the picture, the title with nothing above it, one line: quiet (where it came from, with the platform's mark, and when); with pills (the folder and first tags as pills); marked (the platform's mark on the picture's corner; when and the folder below). The kind shows in the picture: a play mark (tall for reels and shorts), a page and “PDF”, a quote bar, a note's tint, a sound wave, a stack for things saved together; still being read shimmers; couldn't be read says so. For 21 kinds of save, light and dark, and inside today's Library. Then, at Pritam's direction — keep today's style (the caption over the bottom of the picture) but concise, with icons and no tags — two arrangements: concise (the platform's mark and source above the title; icons below for how it was saved, when, the folder) and icons (the title first, then one row of icons).
entries.picked: Today's style, concise — icons instead of words (the platform's own mark, a phone for “iPhone”, a laptop for the browser extension, a folder; a shimmer while it's prepared) and no tags — clean and white, with glass only on the caption: frosted white, the picture softly blurred through it where it overlaps. Glass on the whole card, with colour fields under saves without a picture, was tried and set aside (kept: proposals/cards/GlassEverywhereCard); the card replaced is proposals/cards/BeforeCard. Locked 2026-10-03, with a story for every kind of save (Current/Library card) to refine each later.
entries.why: Pritam: “Today, concise looks good — let's use that, with glass”; then “make the other things colourful”; then “the glass should be white, only on the caption — small kitchen, weeknight tomato rigatoni, 3 days ago kitchen — the rest clean, not a lot of colours”.

entries.title: Search, recent folders and tags, and Kit
entries.question: How do you find what you kept — and where does the agent, Kit, come in?
entries.tried: The kind tabs (links, images, notes, documents) replaced by the folders and tags your saves went into, worked out from the library, newest first, as chips or as “jump back in” cards with each folder's last saves; recent searches as big rows (one tap to run again, one to remove) or chips; and four places for search and Kit: a round search button beside + in the dock; an ask bar (“Search or ask Kit”) always above the dock; Kit in the dock between Gallery and You, where asking is a conversation and typing still searches; a big search field heading the Library. Each in three states — the Library, searching, Kit answering — light and dark. Kit is a stand-in that reads the library on the phone. Then, at Pritam's direction, one field instead of a search/Kit switch — “Search or ask Kit”: a word finds its matches, a question gets a line from Kit above the same results (the backend decides; a stand-in here) — in four places: a search button beside +, the field above the dock, Search as a dock tab, the field heading the Library. Each in three states: the Library, a word, a question.
entries.picked: The field always above the dock, opening at the bottom by the thumb — renamed “Ask Kit” (no “Search”); Jump back in heads the Library. Next: the conversation (2026-10-03-ask-kit).
entries.why: Pritam: “instead of [links, images, notes, documents] show some of the recent tags … or recent collections, dynamic”; “recent searches more accessible”; “something like the + for search”; “a proper agent button … basic search plus agentic search”. Then: “make the search and Ask Kit the same — whenever a user needs to search they activate Kit itself; normal search is handled by the backend; the UI generic and search-based”. Then: “the search panel at the bottom once you open it is nice, easy to access — change it to Ask Kit itself, no need to have Search”.

entries.title: Jump back in
entries.question: What replaces the Library's kind tabs (links, images, notes, documents)?
entries.tried: The folders and tags saves went into, worked out from the library and newest first: as one row of chips (folders with counts, then #tags), or as “Jump back in” — each folder a small card with its last three saves and how many, then the tags as chips. Tapping one shows just its saves.
entries.picked: Jump back in — locked, in every Library design (components/JumpBackIn, collection/places, tested).
entries.why: Pritam: “the jump back in part — collections, tags like cooking — is good; lock this part in all of our designs”.

entries.title: Ask Kit: a conversation
entries.question: How does asking Kit go back and forth — “recent post I saved from Twitter”, then “about cats”?
entries.tried: A follow-up keeps what was asked and changes only what it says (what kind, from where, about what, how recent); when nothing fits, Kit says so and offers what it found elsewhere. Four panels, all from the Ask Kit bar, at the bottom: a conversation with the saves in a row of cards; answers laid out like the Library with earlier turns folded to one line; a half sheet where the Library above becomes the answer; and no bubbles — what Kit understood as chips you can take away, the saves as a list. Each with what-to-ask-next chips over the field, in three states: just opened, one question, a follow-up. Then, at Pritam's direction, two ways in instead of the bar: a plain search button on top (the magnifier opens search in the new design — recent searches and Jump back in, then the saves that match, with “Ask Kit about …” to hand the words to Kit), and Kit beside + in the dock — its logo, or a pill that says “Ask Kit”.
entries.picked: A conversation — your questions and Kit's answers, each answer one short line, a touch larger (“3 posts from X, newest first.” → “1 of them is about cats.”), the saves in a row of the Library's cards — headed “Ask Kit” with the orb, opened from Kit's orb (the logo only) beside + in the dock. Search, from the magnifier on top, locked with its field moved to the bottom. Locked as app components: kit/AskKit, kit/SearchPanel, kit/conversation (tested); not yet in the app's live Library.
entries.why: Pritam: “currently I can't go back and forth … make it conversational; let's design around our search panel now”. Then: “give a basic search button on top as well … and Ask Kit or the Kit logo near the + button at the bottom so they can directly go and ask Kit”. Then: “lock the search panel but move the search bar to the bottom … for Ask Kit we go with A conversation … header Ask Kit with the logo … agent response text short, no clutter, slightly bigger … on our home page the Kit logo only”.

entries.title: The app tour, for a poll on X
entries.question: Which Kit design do people prefer, seen in the whole flow rather than one screen?
entries.tried: The app start to finish, playing by itself in about 24 seconds — sign in with Google, the cards gather while Google opens, the Library loads, a search for “ramen”, then Kit: “recent post I saved from twitter”, then “about cats” — in four versions, one per Kit design: the conversation as locked, answers as a grid, the half sheet, the chips. Filmed frame by frame into one video, four phones side by side (wide) or two by two (tall).
entries.picked: Not picked yet — the four versions go to a poll on X.
entries.why: Pritam: “create a video of our app from auth page to homepage loading, user searching and interacting with Kit … 4 variations, each with their own Kit UI … showing in Storybook first … I'll post on Twitter to keep users engaged”.

entries.title: Home and Ask Kit, closed
entries.question: What are the final home screen and Ask Kit — and what variations of them are worth keeping?
entries.tried: The finals, then variations of each. Home: a greeting (“Good evening, Lena” and your counts in place of “The collection.”), compact (no big title, Jump back in right under the top bar), a nudge (a small card under Jump back in that asks Kit an example question). Ask Kit: the saves as a list under each answer, the best match large with the rest in a row, and a thinking moment (“Looking through your saves…”) before each answer.
entries.picked: Locked. Home: a greeting by name — the time of day, “Hey Lena”, “Welcome back, Lena” — chosen from the day and its part so it holds steady, never past one line (home/greeting, tested), then your counts, Jump back in and the cards; the magnifier on top for Search, Kit's orb beside + for Ask Kit. Ask Kit: a conversation, one short line per answer, the saves as cards that take the width (one spans the row, two share it, more scroll with a hint of the next), the thread blurring under the header and above the field (as the Library's scroll edge; the search panel too). “The collection.” — the first final — and the other variations stay as options.
entries.why: Pritam: “let's close our Ask Kit page design and home screen now — you got both right; give me the final version and some variations as well”. The app tour video is paused for later. Then: “Good morning, Lena is clean, we'll use that — random time-of-day greetings, ‘Hey Pritam’, ‘Welcome back, Pritam’, deterministic, never overflowing; the header/footer progressive blur in Ask Kit too; cards that take the width; and now let's lock this”.

entries.title: Card pictures: one height, then taller up to a most
entries.question: How tall is a card's picture?
entries.tried: Each picture at its own shape (clamped), which left pages and wide photos thin and tall images towering.
entries.picked: A fixed height for a page, a PDF or a full-page screenshot (0.72 of the card's width); a photo or a video at least that tall, taller when it's tall, up to a most (1.35) — collection/preview previewAspect, tested. A post with only words shows its words, not an empty picture.
entries.why: Pritam: “in our card preview let's have a fixed height for image, PDF or page; it expands if there's a very big image, with a max height on it”.

entries.title: A save, opened: With Kit, cleaned
entries.question: What does a save look like when you open it — for every kind of save, from an article to a voice memo?
entries.tried: Four shapes in the locked language, each for fifteen kinds of save (an article, a recipe, a post on X, a post with a photo, a reel, a video, a photo, a screenshot, a full page, a note, a highlight, a PDF, a voice memo, one still being read, one that couldn’t be read). Picture first: the picture, then where it came from, the title, tags, the words, a few facts and related saves; one bar by the thumb with the save’s primary action (“Open on X”, “Open the PDF”, “See it full size”, “Edit the note”), Kit’s orb and more. Reader: the words first, set for reading, a smaller picture, the actions on top. A sheet over the Library: rises from the card you tapped, the Library stays behind. With Kit: ready prompts (Sum it up, More like it, Where is it from?) and “Ask Kit about this save” by the thumb, the answers on the page (kit/aboutSave, tested). In all four: a page’s picture from its top, never cut at the sides; a photo whole; tap for full size; related saves as the Library’s cards, opening in place.
entries.picked: Locked: With Kit, cleaned (proposals/detail/Final.tsx, read through detail/reading, tested). Where it came from and opening it are one line — the platform’s mark, who, when, ↗ — in place of a source line and an “Open on X” pill. A post’s own words lead it, from the copy kept on the server when the save has none; the person’s note sits under them as theirs, never as the title (including notes that had been typed into a post’s title). A link shared from another app as text shows as the link it is (“A YouTube Short”). A summary leads only when it says something new, as a quiet line — no card. Tags, the date, how it was saved and the folder are one quiet block at the bottom. Kit stays by the thumb: Sum it up, More like it, Where is it from?, or your own question, answered on the page. The four shapes stay in Tried/Save detail.
entries.why: Pritam: “we are ready to move to our detailed open view of our saves so we can clean and close that as well”. Today’s screen crops a page’s picture at the sides, puts every part in a frosted panel under uppercase labels, folds where it came from into “Original source”, has four small icons on top and no Kit. Then: “we don’t need to focus on tags or the hashtags — the user doesn’t need to be shown that; show them at the bottom like the Reader variant”. Then, after an audit of his real saves (posts shared from the iPhone showing only his note, links shared as text saved as highlights, notes typed into titles): “the With Kit version is good — focus on our things, clean the UI, merge elements, a clean experience when I open the save; let’s lock it”.
